scored_features.gate_reasoning: G1: iinjurytype appears in the trial_measured_features list so the feature is observed in the data. G2: The hypothesis names a concrete biological pathway (trauma → systemic hyperfibrinolysis amenable to antifibrinolysis with TXA) and contrasts diffuse systemic bleeding vs focal surgically-controlled bleeding, so a mechanistic link is stated. G3: The claim is that blunt multisystem trauma produces systemic fibrinolysis such that TXA changes outcomes differently in that subgroup (a PD/pathophysiologic modifier), not merely an absolute-risk amplifier, so this is a plausible treatment effect modifier. G4: Specific RCT-level evidence for a treatment×injury-type interaction (blunt multisystem vs isolated penetrating) is limited or inconsistent in major trials; therefore the precise interaction is not robustly supported by the published randomized-subgroup literature. G5: Because G4 is judged FALSE the actionable recommendation (prioritise TXA in blunt multisystem when early/no immediate surgery) is not fully literature-backed; therefore G5 is also FALSE (cascade from G4).
scored_features.justification: Decisive gate: G4 FALSE — while the mechanism (systemic fibrinolysis in blunt multisystem trauma) is biologically coherent and plausible as an effect modifier, there is limited RCT subgroup evidence proving a treatment×injury-type interaction, so literature support is insufficient.
